<div class="sheet">

  <div class="ws-head">
    <div>
      <h1>Workload Triage Screen: Does This Work Belong in the Agentic Path?</h1>
      <p class="ws-sub">Panel A, front of card. A triage screen that keeps the pilot backlog free of work the methodology will handle worse than a human would.</p>
    </div>
    <div class="ws-meta">
      <b>WS-27-workload-triage</b><br>
      Pack B - Where we actually are<br>
      fill order <b>4</b> &middot; type <b>decision</b><br>

  </div>

  <div class="ws-source">
    Source: <b>What Comes Next</b>, <i>When NOT to Use Agentic Workflows</i> &middot;
    <code>handbook/ch27-what-comes-next.qmd</code> L129-143 &middot; ch10 L88-120 &middot;
    <a href="https://danielmeppiel.github.io/agentic-sdlc-handbook/handbook/ch27-what-comes-next.html#sec-next-when-not-to-use">#sec-next-when-not-to-use</a>
  </div>

  <div class="ws-instruction">
    <b>One card per backlog item. Print the deck from fifteen to twenty real items.</b>
    Write the item, then run it past the five exclusions. Tick an exclusion only if it applies to this item.
    Turn the card over for the three gates and the routing, then drop it on the matching pile.
    The tech lead who owns the backlog holds the pen, with a senior engineer who will run the agents.
  </div>

  <div class="ws-block">
    <h2>Panel A &mdash; the triage screen <span class="ws-block-note">one row per candidate work item &middot; exclusions 1-5</span></h2>
    <table class="ws">
      <colgroup>
        <col style="width:6%"><col style="width:20%"><col style="width:46%"><col style="width:28%">
      </colgroup>
      <thead>
        <tr><th></th><th>Column</th><th>What the book says</th><th>Your answer</th></tr>
      </thead>
      <tbody>
        <tr>
          <td class="ws-num"><span class="fno">1</span></td>
          <td><b>Work item ID and title</b></td>
          <td class="prior">&mdash;</td>
          <td class="fill"><span class="f-text"></span></td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <td class="ws-num"><span class="fno">2</span></td>
          <td><b>Selected how</b></td>
          <td class="prior">Recorded once for the sample, printed on the tally sheet.<span class="prior-src">derived</span></td>
          <td class="fill">
            <div class="f-select"><span class="opt">random</span><span class="opt">stratified</span><span class="opt">hand-picked</span></div>
          </td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <td class="ws-num"><span class="fno">3</span></td>
          <td><b>Exclusion 1 &mdash; fewer than 50 lines of change?</b></td>
          <td class="prior">If you can hold the full scope in your head, the overhead of persona design, wave planning and checkpoint discipline is not worth it. Just write the code.<span class="prior-src">ch27 L131</span></td>
          <td class="fill"><span class="f-checkline"><span class="f-check"></span>applies</span></td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <td class="ws-num"><span class="fno">4</span></td>
          <td><b>Exclusion 2 &mdash; domain knowledge entirely implicit?</b></td>
          <td class="prior">Conventions, constraints and trade-offs that cannot be externalised into instruction files, because they depend on political context, unwritten relationships or organisational history. <b>Routes to instrumentation, not rejection.</b><span class="prior-src">ch27 L133</span></td>
          <td class="fill"><span class="f-checkline"><span class="f-check"></span>applies</span></td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <td class="ws-num"><span class="fno">5</span></td>
          <td><b>Exclusion 3 &mdash; failure cost low and iteration cheap?</b></td>
          <td class="prior">Throwaway scripts, prototyping, exploratory work: a single agent prompt with no orchestration is faster and sufficient.<span class="prior-src">ch27 L135</span></td>
          <td class="fill"><span class="f-checkline"><span class="f-check"></span>applies</span></td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <td class="ws-num"><span class="fno">6</span></td>
          <td><b>Exclusion 4 &mdash; inherently sequential and judgment-dense?</b></td>
          <td class="prior">Naming things, choosing abstractions, defining API contracts. "Use agents as sounding boards, not as orchestrated fleets."<span class="prior-src">ch27 L137</span></td>
          <td class="fill"><span class="f-checkline"><span class="f-check"></span>applies</span></td>
        </tr>
        <tr>
          <td class="ws-num"><span class="fno">7</span></td>
          <td><b>Exclusion 5 &mdash; the platform fights automation?</b></td>
          <td class="prior">The platform's internals are undocumented and hostile to external manipulation. Escalate to a human with a precise checklist rather than attempting a fourth approach.<span class="prior-src">ch27 L139</span></td>
          <td class="fill"><span class="f-checkline"><span class="f-check"></span>applies</span></td>
        </tr>
      </tbody>
    </table>
  </div>

          <td class="fill"><div class="f-select"><span class="opt">Agentic now</span><span class="opt">Split</span><span class="opt">Instrument first</span><span class="opt">Keep manual</span></div></td>
